_comment:
The noise floor — the number below which no delta is a result. Stage 0, and it is first because everything downstream quotes it.

Measured by running the SAME weights through the SAME measurement twice and taking the spread. Both are ordinary `/eval-run` runs; this file cites them rather than holding a number somebody typed. The recorded cost of getting this wrong: a floor reported as 0.06 that was really 0.25, a "+0.30 is real" conclusion built on it, and the whole thing withdrawn.
_comment_value: The spread between the repeat measurements, in the metric's own unit. ‼️ It is a DERIVED number, not a transcribed one, and that distinction is the whole shape of `sources` here: no evaluation log anywhere prints a spread, so there is nothing to transcribe. Write a RULER — a small re-runnable script (`stages/exploration/scripts/<name>.py`) that reads the two runs' metric lines and prints every delta — and cite it as `{ref: <the script>, command: <how to run it>, quote: <its stdout>, kind: 'derived'}`, beside the two endpoint log lines cited `kind: 'result'` as usual. Then the floor has a source that can be RE-RUN: change the weights and you re-run the ruler instead of hand-editing this file. ‼️ Do NOT write a `quote` like "31.09 - 28.16 = 2.93" — an arithmetic sentence nobody printed is exactly the fabrication `graph.py check` exists to catch, and `derived` exists so that the honest record is also the cheap one. Full rule in `state.json -> _comment_constants`. A floor is what every later verdict rests on, so it is the last number that may be typed from memory. `null` means NOT MEASURED — which is a different fact from zero and must never be rendered as one. While it is null, no card may report a result as anything but `[T1 trend]`: "no significant improvement" is UNDECIDABLE without a floor, not a negative.
_comment_origin: Where this number was measured, and therefore what may be asked of it. `mlclaw` (the default — an absent field reads as this, so every record written before the field existed stays valid) means this project measured it, and `runs` below names the repeat measurements `graph.py check` re-reads. `external` means it was measured somewhere MLClaw cannot re-read: before the takeover, on a box that has since been released, by a pipeline that never wrote a `run.json`. ‼️ That case is the NORMAL way in, not the exception — `SKILL.md -> Where you come in` says so in its own heading — and until `external` existed the only writable forms were a null floor or two invented run ids, of which the record layer rewarded the invented one. An external floor is a `claim` (MLClaw's existing word, the same one `conclude.py` gives an external reference): it still gates T2, it can NEVER carry a T3, and `sources` is enforced exactly as it is for a measured floor — so a number nobody can quote still cannot be written here.
_comment_runs: The two (or more) `/eval-run` run ids the floor was computed from, when `origin` is `mlclaw`. Two ids that differ in anything but the seed do not measure a noise floor — they measure that difference. `graph.py check` re-reads their `run.json` and refuses a floor whose runs disagree on `mode`, `scope`, or dataset identity. ‼️ Ids that do not resolve leave the floor `unverifiable`, which gates no further than `external` does: inventing two is not a way to buy a stronger floor, and it never was a way to buy an honest one. Leave this empty for an external floor — naming both is two accounts of where the number came from, and only one can be true.
_comment_unchecked: Required when `origin` is `external`, ignored otherwise. One sentence: what nobody in this project could confirm, and why it cannot simply be re-measured here. ‼️ The first half is always the same — nothing here can confirm the two measurements differed only in the seed — so the half that earns its place is the second: the box was released, the checkpoint is on a powered-down disk, it predates MLClaw. That is what the next reader needs in order to decide whether to spend two `/eval-run`s and replace this with a measured one. A floor that cannot say it is treated as NOT MEASURED; the door is narrow on purpose.
_comment_sources: Grounding for `value`, per `_comment_value`: the endpoint log lines (`kind: 'result'`) plus the ruler that computed the spread (`kind: 'derived'`, which additionally requires `command`). ‼️ With a `derived` source present, only IT must quote the number — the endpoints are its inputs. Without one, every source must quote it, which is why citing the two logs alone can never satisfy this field: neither log contains the difference.
_comment_measured_on: Which corpus. A floor is a property of (weights × measurement × corpus), not of the model — changing any of the three retires it. Must equal `graph.json -> corpus`.
_comment_retires_on: ‼️ Stated up front, because the rule is otherwise remembered rather than executed: change the metric, the renderer, or the frame selection and the old curve is void. A day-over-day delta that spans one of these is not a model delta, and reading it as one produces a whole overfitting story about a rendering change.
